334592.title: Bijection conjecture for hesitating walks and excursions in the octant and quadrant
334592.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer. A **hesitating excursion** is a hesitating walk of length $2n$ in the quadrant that returns to its starting point, and a **hesitating axis-walk** is a hesitating walk of length $2n$ in the octant constrained to the axis. The **thick diagonal** is

$$
\{(n,n),n\in\mathbb{N}\}\bigcup\{(n+1,n),n\in\mathbb{N}\}.
$$

**Bijection conjecture.** The following families are in bijection: hesitating excursions of length $2n$ in the quadrant; hesitating axis-walks of length $2n$ in the octant; and hesitating walks of length $2n$ in the octant ending on the thick diagonal.

The first two families are already known to be equinumerous with Baxter numbers, while the computational enumeration mentioned in the source suggests the bijective link with hesitating walks ending on the thick diagonal. The conjecture concerns the existence of bijections among all three families.

334668.title: The combinatorial non-crossing-sums inequality
334668.literal_statement:
Let $k_1,k_2,k_3$ be odd natural numbers. For each $i=1,2,3$, let $y_{i,1},\ldots,y_{i,k_i}$ be distinct real numbers, and set $y_{i,0}=y_{i,k_i+1}=-\infty$. For two finite pairs of real numbers, call their sums non-crossing when the two sums of one choice and the two sums of the other choice do not alternate in order. Assume:

1. For each $1\le i\le3$ and $0\le p<q\le k_i$ of the same parity, the pairs $\{y_{i,p},y_{i,p+1}\}$ and $\{-y_{i,q},-y_{i,q+1}\}$ have non-crossing sums.
2. For $0\le p_i\le k_i$ of the same parity, the three pairs $\{y_{1,p_1},y_{1,p_1+1}\}$, $\{y_{2,p_2},y_{2,p_2+1}\}$, and $\{y_{3,p_3},y_{3,p_3+1}\}$ have non-crossing sums.

**Combinatorial formulation conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum_{i=1}^3\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}(-1)^{j-1}y_{i,j}<0.
$$

This is an almost purely combinatorial formulation of the symmetric area inequality. It is stated as an open conjecture in the paper.

334897.title: The looped-path sorting conjecture
334897.literal_statement:
Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle$ be the graph obtained from the infinite path $\mathbb{Z}$ by adding one loop at each vertex in $S$. For a chip configuration $\mathcal{C}$, write $\widetilde{\mathcal{C}}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle}$ for its stable stabilization on this graph. Suppose $n\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{min}(\widetilde{n\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})<\mathrm{min}(\widetilde{(n-1)\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})
$$

and

$$
\mathrm{max}(\widetilde{n\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle})>\mathrm{max}(\widetilde{(n-1)\delta_0}^{\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle}).
$$

**Looped-path sorting conjecture.** Then $\mathbb{Z}\langle S\rangle$ sorts $\Delta^n$. Here, sorting means that every labeled stabilization of the initial configuration $\Delta^n$ is in sorted order. This generalizes the main sorting theorem for the infinite path and includes the cases $S=\varnothing$ and $S=\{0\}$, while the general balanced-loop case remains open.

329781.title: Faben–Jerrum dichotomy conjecture for homomorphisms to graphs modulo 2
329781.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. An **involution-free reduction** of $H$ is the unique, up to isomorphism, involution-free graph $H^*$ such that $H\Rightarrow^* H^*$, where $H\Rightarrow^* H'$ denotes a sequence of reductions by taking the subgraph induced by the fixed points of a nontrivial involutive automorphism, up to isomorphism. Write $\oplus\operatorname{HomsTo}(H)$ for the problem of counting homomorphisms from an input graph to $H$, modulo $2$.

**Faben–Jerrum's conjecture.** Let $H$ be a graph. If its involution-free reduction $H^*$ has at most one vertex, then $\oplus\operatorname{HomsTo}(H)$ is in $\mathrm{P}$; otherwise, $\oplus\operatorname{HomsTo}(H)$ is $\oplus\mathrm{P}$-complete.

This conjecture predicts a complete polynomial-time versus $\oplus\mathrm{P}$-complete dichotomy for counting graph homomorphisms modulo $2$. Faben and Jerrum established the existence and uniqueness of the involution-free reduction; the dichotomy asserted here is the remaining complexity classification.

330225.title: Factorization conjecture for weighted Aztec-region matching generating functions
330225.literal_statement:
Let $x,y,z$ be indeterminate edge weights, and let $A^{(i)}_{a,b,c}(x,y,z)$ and $F^{(i)}_{a,b,c}(x,y,z)$, for $i=1,2,3$, be the corresponding weighted versions of the graphs $A^{(i)}_{a,b,c}$ and $F^{(i)}_{a,b,c}$. Define

$$
\alpha(a,b,c;x,y,z)
$$

and

$$
\beta(a,b,c;x,y,z)
$$

by the piecewise formulas given in the source. **Factorization conjecture.** The matching generating functions of the weighted graphs $A^{(i)}_{a,b,c}(x,y,z)$ all have the form

$$
\alpha(a,b,c;x,y,z)2^{X}(x^2+2xyz+2y^2z^2)^{Y}(2x^2+5xyz+4y^2z^2)^{Z}x^{T}y^{Q}z^{K},
$$

for some $X,Y,Z,T,Q,K$ depending only on $a,b,c$. Similarly, the matching generating functions of the weighted graphs $F^{(i)}_{a,b,c}(x,y,z)$ all have the form

$$
\beta(a,b,c;x,y,z)2^{X'}(x^2+2xyz+2y^2z^2)^{Y'}(2x^2+5xyz+4y^2z^2)^{Z'}x^{T'}y^{Q'}z^{K'},
$$

for some $X',Y',Z',T',Q',K'$ depending only on $a,b,c$. The proposed factorization captures the observed structure of these matching generating functions; the supplied text gives no resolution.

330246.title: Weighted average-size conjecture for self-conjugate core partitions
330246.literal_statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be coprime positive integers. Write $\mathcal{D}_s$ for the set of self-conjugate $s$-cores, let $\mathcal{D}_t$ be the set of self-conjugate $t$-cores, and let $\operatorname{StabSC}_{s,t}(\lambda)$ be the stabiliser of $\lambda\in\mathcal{D}_s\cap\mathcal{D}_t$ under the level-$t$ action of $\widetilde{\mathfrak H}_s$ on $\mathcal{D}_s$.

**Weighted self-conjugate core-average conjecture.**

$$
\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}_s\cap\mathcal{D}_t}\frac{|\lambda|}{|\operatorname{StabSC}_{s,t}(\lambda)|}}{\displaystyle\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal{D}_s\cap\mathcal{D}_t}\frac{1}{|\operatorname{StabSC}_{s,t}(\lambda)|}}=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{(s-1)(t^2-1)}{24} & \text{if } t \text{ is odd},\\[9pt]
\dfrac{(s-1)(t^2+2)}{24} & \text{if } t \text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is the self-conjugate analogue of the weighted core-average conjecture, incorporating the parity of $t$. The supplied text does not state a resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

330257.title: The rational Catalan length-skew-length conjecture for core partitions
330257.literal_statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime positive integers. An $(m,n)$-core is a partition that is simultaneously an $m$-core and an $n$-core; denote the set of such cores by $\mathcal P_{m,n}$. Let $\ell(\lambda)$ and $s\ell(\lambda)$ be the length and skew-length statistics of an $(m,n)$-core $\lambda$. Define $[a]_q=1+q+\cdots+q^{a-1}$ and $\left[m+n \atop m,n \right]_q$ as the relevant $q$-multinomial coefficient. **The rational Catalan length-skew-length conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal P_{m,n}}q^{\ell(\lambda)+s\ell(\lambda)}=\operatorname{Cat}_{m,n}(q)=\frac{1}{[m+n]_q}\left[m+n \atop m,n \right]_q.
$$

This is the core-partition formulation of a combinatorial interpretation for the rational Catalan polynomial. The source attributes it to Armstrong and collaborators and gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

330411.title: Chen–Han–O–Shan–Tsuchiya conjecture on spanning Halin subgraphs
330411.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a forbidden pair, meaning a family of two forbidden subgraphs. For two families $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$ of forbidden subgraphs, write $\mathcal{H}_1\leq\mathcal{H}_2$ if every $H_2\in\mathcal{H}_2$ contains some $H_1\in\mathcal{H}_1$ as an induced subgraph. A graph is **$\mathcal{H}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{H}$. A **spanning Halin subgraph** is a spanning subgraph that is a Halin graph, where a Halin graph is formed from a tree without vertices of degree $2$ and a cycle induced by the leaves of that tree. Let $K_{1,3}$ be the claw, and let $Z_3$ and $B_{1,2}$ denote the forbidden graphs used in the source. **Chen–Han–O–Shan–Tsuchiya conjecture.** Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a forbidden pair. Every $3$-connected $\mathcal{H}$-free graph has a spanning Halin subgraph if and only if either

$$
\mathcal{H}\leq\{K_{1,3},Z_3\}
$$

or

$$
\mathcal{H}\leq\{K_{1,3},B_{1,2}\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a complete characterization of the forbidden pairs guaranteeing a spanning Halin subgraph in every $3$-connected graph in the corresponding hereditary class; the supplied text gives no resolution status or additional partial results.

330708.title: A multi-sequence formula for the Möbius function of the permutation poset
330708.literal_statement:
Let $\pi=\pi_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\pi_n$ be a decomposable permutation with $t$ sequences of equal components

$$
\pi_{s_i+1}=\cdots=\pi_{s_i+\alpha_i}\ne 1
$$

of respective lengths $\alpha_i$, for $1\le i\le t$. Let $\lambda=\lambda_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\lambda_m$ be obtained from $\pi$ by reducing the $i$-th sequence to length $\ell_i$, where $0\le \ell_i\le \alpha_i$. Write $\alpha=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_t$ and $\ell=\ell_1+\cdots+\ell_t$. **The multi-sequence Möbius formula.** The alternating sum over normal embeddings satisfies

$$
\sum_{S\in EZ^{\lambda,\pi}}(-1)^{|S|}=(-1)^{\alpha-\ell-1}\prod_{i=1}^t\binom{\alpha_i-1}{\ell_i-1}.
$$

This conjecture extends the formula for removing elements from a single sequence of equal components in the decomposable permutation $\pi$. It gives an explicit product formula for the relevant alternating sum, and hence is intended to describe the Möbius function of the interval $[\lambda,\pi]$ when several equal-component sequences are reduced simultaneously. Its resolution is not established by the supplied context.

330849.title: Smoothness conjecture for complete pointsets in gauged linear sigma-models
330849.literal_statement:
Let ${\Scr A}$ and ${\Scr B}$ be pointsets defining a gauged linear $\sigma$-model. The pair is **${\Scr B}$-complete** when

$$
\operatorname{Conv}\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Conv}{\Scr A})^\vee\cap M\cap H_\nu\bigr)=\operatorname{Conv}({\Scr B}),
$$

and **${\Scr A}$-complete** when

$$
\operatorname{Conv}\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Conv}{\Scr B})^\vee\cap N\cap H_\mu\bigr)=\operatorname{Conv}({\Scr A}).
$$

**Smoothness conjecture.** If a gauged linear $\sigma$-model is defined by pointsets ${\Scr A}$ and ${\Scr B}$ which are both ${\Scr A}$-complete and ${\Scr B}$-complete, then this model is nonsingular for generic values of the complex-structure and Kähler parameters.

The conjecture proposes that imposing both completeness conditions prevents singularities after the extremal transitions used to enlarge the pointsets. The source gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.

331026.title: Busch–Ferrara–Hartke–Jacobson–Kaul–West conjecture on edge-disjoint perfect matchings
331026.literal_statement:
Let $\pi=(d_1,d_2,\ldots,d_n)$ be a degree sequence, and let $\pi-k=(d_1-k,d_2-k,\ldots,d_n-k)$. A sequence is **graphic** if it is the degree sequence of a graph, and $\pi$ **potentially has** a property if some realization of $\pi$ has that property. A $1$-factor is a perfect matching. The sequence $\pi$ has **even length** when $n$ is even.

**Busch–Ferrara–Hartke–Jacobson–Kaul–West conjecture.** The sequences $\pi$ and $\pi-k$ are graphic and of even length if and only if $\pi$ potentially has $k$ edge-disjoint $1$-factors.

This conjecture strengthens Kundu's theorem, which characterizes when a graphic degree sequence potentially has a $k$-factor by the graphicness of $\pi-k$. The paper introduces a multi-switch and proves weaker decompositions, but the stated equivalence is not resolved in the supplied text.

331721.title: Correct-path survival conjecture for split-reduced successive cancellation list decoding
331721.literal_statement:
A polar code is decoded using a split-reduced successive cancellation list decoder, with $u_i$ denoting the current unfrozen bit and $P_e(u_i)$ its decoding error probability. Under the Gaussian approximation, consider a correct decoding path that survives through $u_1^{i-1}$.

**Correct-path survival conjecture.** As $P_e(u_i)$ approaches zero, with high probability the current path survives at $u_i$ without splitting and $u_i$ is correctly decoded. If the subsequent subchannels corresponding to $u_{i+1}^N$ become increasingly reliable, then the correct path survives until termination without splitting with high probability.

This conjecture concerns the path behavior induced by the proposed split-reduced rule; the paper reports empirical evidence for it, while a quantitative result is difficult because list-decoding pruning couples exponentially many error patterns.

332073.title: Optimality conjecture for the local-set-based piecewise-constant wavelet basis
332073.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{W}$ be the local-set-based wavelet basis with the even partition. For a fixed sparsity level $K$, consider signals $\mathbf{x}$ satisfying

$$
\left\|\Delta\mathbf{x}\right\|_0\leq K.
$$

**Optimality conjecture.** The local-set-based wavelet basis $\operatorname{W}_{\rm LSPC}$ minimizes, among all orthonormal bases $\operatorname{F}$, the worst-case number of nonzero coefficients:

$$
\operatorname{W}_{\rm LSPC}=\arg\min_{\operatorname{F}}\ \max_{\mathbf{x}:\,\left\|\Delta\mathbf{x}\right\|_0\leq K}\left\|\operatorname{F}^T\mathbf{x}\right\|_0,
$$

subject to $\operatorname{F}$ being orthonormal. The conjecture asserts that this construction is optimal for promoting sparsity in piecewise-constant graph signals; the surrounding discussion establishes sparsity bounds for the proposed basis but provides no resolution of this global optimality claim.

326986.title: Conjectures on Hamilton cycles in regular directed and oriented graphs
326986.literal_statement:
A $D$-regular directed graph is a digraph in which every vertex has in-degree and out-degree equal to $D$, and an **oriented graph** is a digraph without $2$-cycles.

**Conjectures on Hamilton cycles in regular directed and oriented graphs.**

(a) For each $D>2$, every $D$-regular oriented graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with

$$
D\geq \frac{n-1}{4}
$$

is Hamiltonian.

(b) Every strongly $2$-connected $D$-regular digraph on $n$ vertices with

$$
D\geq \frac{n}{3}
$$

is Hamiltonian.

(c) For each $D>2$, every $D$-regular strongly $2$-connected oriented graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with

$$
D\geq \frac{n}{6}
$$

is Hamiltonian.

These are directed analogues of Hamilton-cycle questions for connected regular graphs. The source attributes (a) to Jackson and says that (b) and (c) were raised in a survey; their general status is not resolved in the supplied text.

327053.title: The first-two-layers conjecture for spherical designs of Euclidean lattices
327053.literal_statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a lattice, and let $M_1(\Lambda)$ and $M_2(\Lambda)$ denote its first and second layers. A finite subset of a sphere is a **spherical $2$-design** when it satisfies the defining moment conditions for a spherical $2$-design. **First-two-layers conjecture.** If the first two layers $M_1(\Lambda)$ and $M_2(\Lambda)$ of $\Lambda$ are spherical $2$-designs, then all the other layers are $2$-designs; in particular, $\Lambda$ is fully critical for the height $h$. The conjecture would extend the observed phenomenon that, for the strongly eutactic lattices examined by the authors up to dimension $8$, failure of full criticality is already detected in the second layer. It would also provide a sufficient criterion for full criticality beyond the condition established by the paper's theorem; the general assertion remains open in the supplied source.

327186.title: The index conjecture for minimal zero-sum sequences of length four
327186.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite cyclic group such that $\gcd(|G|,6)=1$. A **minimal zero-sum sequence** over $G$ is a finite sequence whose sum is zero but no proper nontrivial subsequence has sum zero. For a sequence $S=(n_1g)\cdot\ldots\cdot(n_kg)$ over $G$, with $1\leq n_1,\ldots,n_k\leq |G|$ and $g$ a generator of $G$, define

$$
\operatorname{ind}(S)=\min_{\langle g\rangle=G}\frac{n_1+\cdots+n_k}{\operatorname{ord}(g)}.
$$

**The index conjecture.** Every minimal zero-sum sequence $S$ over $G$ of length $|S|=4$ has

$$
\operatorname{ind}(S)=1.
$$

This is the length-four case of the index conjecture for minimal zero-sum sequences in finite cyclic groups of order coprime to $6$. The paper states that the general conjecture holds for reduced sequences satisfying the (A1) condition, but the supplied text gives no resolution status for the length-four assertion.

327948.title: The conjectural generating-series formula for minimal transitive cycle factorizations with three cycles
327948.literal_statement:
Let $c_{{\alpha}\,;\,{\beta}}$ be the number of minimal transitive cycle factorizations with signature ${\beta}$ of a permutation with cycle type ${\alpha}$. Define

$$
\Psi_m({\mathbf{x}},{\mathbf{q}})=\sum_{{\alpha},{\beta}}c_{{\alpha}\,;\,{\beta}}\frac{1}{|{\beta}|!}\frac{x_1^{{\alpha}_1}\cdots x_m^{{\alpha}_m}}{{\alpha}_1\cdots {\alpha}_m}{\mathbf{q}}^{{\beta}}.
$$

Let $w=w(x,\mathbf q)$ be the unique solution of $w=xe^{Q(w)}$, set $T(w)=1-wQ'(w)$, and write $w_i=w(x_i,\mathbf q)$, $Q_i=Q(w_i)$, and $T_i=T(w_i)$ for $i=1,2,3$.

**Conjectural formula for $\Psi_3$.** With this notation,

$$
\Psi_{3}=w_1w_2w_3\sum_{i=1}^{3}\frac{1}{T_i}\prod_{j\ne i}\frac{Q_i-Q_j}{(w_i-w_j)^2}.
$$

The formula is motivated by the close parallel between the known expressions for inequivalent factorizations and the corresponding generating series for ordinary minimal transitive cycle factorizations. The source presents it as a conjectural form; no resolution is supplied.

327985.title: Best monotone condition for 2-factor graphs to be Hamiltonian
327985.literal_statement:
Let $\pi=(d_1\le\cdots\le d_n)$ be a graphical degree sequence, and let $G$ be a realization of $\pi$. Say that $G$ **contains a $2$-factor** if it has a spanning $2$-regular subgraph, and say that $G$ is **hamiltonian** if it contains a cycle through all its vertices. The degree condition in Theorem 45 is the condition

$$
d_i\le i\;\Rightarrow\;d_{n-i}\ge n-i,\quad 1\le i\le\tfrac12(n-3),
$$

$$
d_{i-1}\le i\;\Rightarrow\;d_{n-i}\ge\tfrac12(n+1),\quad 1\le i\le\tfrac12(n-5),\text{ if }n\text{ is odd},
$$

$$
d_{i-1}\le i\;\Rightarrow\;d_{n/2-1}\ge\tfrac12n\;\vee\;d_{n-i}\ge\tfrac12n+1,\quad 1\le i\le\tfrac12(n-4),\text{ if }n\text{ is even}.
$$

**2-factor Hamiltonicity conjecture.** This degree condition is a best monotone degree condition for $2$-factor $\Rightarrow$ hamiltonian. The source states that a best monotone condition for this implication is not currently known; the conjecture remains open.
